text: Figure reference: phylum-level xoxF-versus-mxaF comparison on a log scale.
quote: ![xoxF vs mxaF by phylum (log scale)](figures/xoxF_vs_mxaF_by_phylum.png)
heading: 1. xoxF (REE-dependent MDH) outnumbers mxaF (Ca-dependent MDH) by ~19:1 across the BERDL pangenome — H1 strongly supported

text: In 293,059 GTDB-r214 genomes, eggNOG annotated xoxF/K00114 in 3,690 and mxaF/K14028 in 195: ratio 18.92:1 (Clopper–Pearson 95% CI [13.07, 27.69]); xoxF fraction 0.9498 (95% CI [0.9425, 0.9558]); the preregistered one-sided test gave p = 7.6 × 10⁻²².
quote: Across 293,059 GTDB-r214 genomes, eggNOG `KEGG_ko = K00114` (xoxF, lanthanide-dependent methanol dehydrogenase, EC 1.1.2.8) is annotated in **3,690 genomes**, while `K14028` (mxaF, Ca-dependent methanol dehydrogenase, EC 1.1.2.7) is annotated in **195 genomes** — a global xoxF:mxaF ratio of **18.92 : 1**, with a Clopper-Pearson 95% CI of [13.07, 27.69]. The xoxF fraction of joint MDH calls (xoxF + mxaF) is **0.9498** [95% CI 0.9425, 0.9558]. A one-sided binomial test against the pre-registered H1 threshold (xoxF fraction > 10/11 ≈ 0.909) gives **p = 7.6 × 10⁻²²**. **H1 is strongly supported.**
heading: 1. xoxF (REE-dependent MDH) outnumbers mxaF (Ca-dependent MDH) by ~19:1 across the BERDL pangenome — H1 strongly supported

text: The directional xoxF-dominance result survived Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction across 29 testable phyla with MDH calls and adequate sample size.
quote: After Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction across 29 testable phyla, the directional H1 verdict survives in every phylum that has any MDH calls and adequate sample size: Pseudomonadota, Acidobacteriota, Actinomycetota, Bacteroidota, Campylobacterota, Verrucomicrobiota, Chloroflexota, Gemmatimonadota, Methylomirabilota, Halobacteriota archaea, Thermoproteota archaea, and others.
heading: 1. xoxF (REE-dependent MDH) outnumbers mxaF (Ca-dependent MDH) by ~19:1 across the BERDL pangenome — H1 strongly supported

heading: Phylogenetic-correction validation (NB08)

text: The naive genome-level analysis used 3,885 units and estimated an xoxF fraction of 0.950 with 95% CI [0.942, 0.956].
quote: | NB03 naive pooled (genome-level) | 3,885 | 0.950 | [0.942, 0.956] | ✅ |
heading: Phylogenetic-correction validation (NB08)

text: Equal weighting of 271 GTDB families gave an xoxF fraction of 0.960 with 95% CI [0.941, 0.976].
quote: | NB08 family-level equal-weight (each GTDB family = 1 unit) | 271 | 0.960 | [0.941, 0.976] | ✅ |
heading: Phylogenetic-correction validation (NB08)

text: The Bayesian binomial mixed model with phylum and family effects used 3,885 units and estimated an xoxF fraction of 0.993 with interval [0.992, 0.994].
quote: | NB08 Bayesian binomial GLMM with `(1\|phylum) + (1\|family)` | 3,885 | **0.993** | [0.992, 0.994] | ✅ |
heading: Phylogenetic-correction validation (NB08)

text: A variational-Bayes binomial mixed model with phylum and family random intercepts yielded an approximately 143:1 xoxF:mxaF ratio (95% credible interval [122, 169]); a bootstrap equally weighting 271 informative families yielded 0.960 [0.941, 0.976].
quote: The GLMM (variational-Bayes binomial GLMM via `statsmodels.BinomialBayesMixedGLM`, with random intercepts for phylum and family) gives the *strongest* xoxF dominance signal — a phylogeny-corrected ratio of **~143 : 1** with 95% credible interval [122, 169] — because the random effects absorb phylum-level heterogeneity and reveal that *within typical phyla*, xoxF dominance is more extreme than the global pooled estimate suggests. The family-equal-weight bootstrap (each of 271 MDH-informative GTDB families counted once regardless of genome count) gives 0.960 [0.941, 0.976], confirming H1 is not driven by Pseudomonadota's 117 K-genome size advantage. **H1 is robust to all three phylogenetic-correction frameworks.**
heading: Phylogenetic-correction validation (NB08)

text: The report grades H2 as partially supported: soil/sediment and marine enrichment and host-associated depletion passed its correction, while the n=37 REE-impacted elevation did not pass the false-discovery-rate threshold (p_BH = 0.082).
quote: **H2 is partially supported.** Soil/sediment is by far the strongest broad-class enrichment (OR=1.92, p_BH=6×10⁻³⁹ across 13,779 genomes), consistent with methanol oxidation as a known soil microbial process and the reservoir of lanthanide minerals in soil. Marine environments are also significantly enriched (OR=1.31). REE-impacted samples (n=37) show a 3.5-fold descriptive elevation (10.8 % vs 3.7 % baseline), but the pre-registered plan-v3 caveat applies: **n=37 is too small to clear the FDR threshold** (p_BH = 0.082). Host-associated environments are dramatically *depleted* in xoxF (OR=0.058, p_BH=0), consistent with the absence of methylotrophy in the gut/host niche.

quote: The 37 metagenome-assembled genomes from samples explicitly tagged `isolation_source = "rare earth elements-acid mine drainage (REEs-AMD) contaminated river water"` (BioSamples SAMN16745347-...; MIMAG.water.6.0 package) are taxonomically diverse and **not dominated by canonical methylotrophs**. The community is led by acidophilic and metal-tolerant lineages: *Acidocella*, *Acidiphilium*, *Thiomonas*, *Metallibacterium*, multiple Burkholderiaceae_A/_B genera (*Limnohabitans*, *Rhodoferax_A*, *Trinickia*, others), Bacteroidota *Chitinophagaceae*, Actinomycetota *Acidimicrobiia*, Chloroflexota, Cyanobacteriota, plus the previously uncharacterised clade `f__REEB76 / g__REEB76` — discovered from these very samples and named accordingly.

text: Only 4/37 REE-acid-mine-drainage MAGs carried xoxF and 0/37 carried bakta-validated lanmodulin or xoxJ. DNA-repair, acid-resistance, metal-response, and oxidative-stress products were more prevalent; every listed product count is out of 37 MAGs.
quote: Only **4/37** REE-AMD MAGs carry any xoxF; **0/37** carry bakta-validated lanmodulin or xoxJ. The functional signature instead reads as a textbook acid-mine-drainage stress profile: high prevalence of DNA-repair enzymes (RecN 33, RadA 32, RecO 31, RecA 28, RadC 24), acid-resistance machinery (FtsH zinc metalloprotease 31, proton-translocating NAD(P)+ transhydrogenase 27), MerR-family heavy-metal-responsive transcriptional regulators (30), and oxidative-stress defense (thioredoxin reductase 25, glutathione peroxidase 24). Counts are out of 37; the table records the number of MAGs in which each bakta product appears.

quote: 59 % of xoxF-without-PQQ cases are eggNOG annotation gaps that bakta detects; the remaining ~24 % of xoxF carriers genuinely lack PQQ evidence
heading: Novel Contribution

text: Three H1 validations had 95 % CI lower bounds above the 10 : 1 threshold; the binomial mixed model gave a ratio of ~143 : 1.
quote: All three confirm H1 with 95 % CI lower bounds above the 10 : 1 threshold; the GLMM gives a phylogeny-corrected ratio of ~143 : 1.
heading: Limitations

text: H2 environmental analyses were stratified within phyla but not assessed with a fully phylogeny-aware mixed model.
quote: **H2 still relies on within-phylum stratified analyses rather than a fully phylogeny-aware mixed model**
heading: Limitations

text: Marker calls differed substantially between eggNOG and bakta; headline statistics used marker-specific calibration, with secondary source-union analyses.
quote: eggNOG and bakta calls disagree substantially for several markers (xoxJ, lanmodulin, PQQ biosynthesis). Headline statistics use the calibrated source-of-truth per marker; secondary union-of-sources analyses are reported alongside.
heading: Limitations

text: The REE-AMD evidence is descriptive only: n=37 from one bioproject, not a basis for environmental inference.
quote: **REE-AMD anchor is small (n=37) and from a single bioproject**: descriptive only. Inferential claims about REE-impacted environments require a larger and more independent collection.
heading: Limitations

text: AlphaEarth covered 39.5 % (1,457 / 3,690) xoxF genomes versus a 28 % pangenome baseline; 60.5 % lacked coordinates.
quote: **AlphaEarth coverage of xoxF genomes is 39.5 %** (1,457 / 3,690) — better than the 28 % pangenome baseline, but still leaves 60.5 % of xoxF carriers without environmental coordinates.
heading: Limitations

text: AlphaEarth is the environmental-coordinate dataset assessed for xoxF genomes.
quote: AlphaEarth coverage of xoxF genomes is 39.5 %
heading: Limitations

text: The report did not perform embedding-based niche analysis; a supplementary analysis restricted to genomes with environmental coordinates remains feasible.
quote: Embedding-based niche analysis was scoped out of this report; coverage-restricted supplementary analysis is feasible.
heading: Limitations

text: Environmental categories derive from ncbi_env text mining and broad host-associated regexes; misclassification is possible despite reported soil/sediment enrichment and host depletion.
quote: **`ncbi_env` environmental classification is text-mining-derived** with hierarchical regex priorities. The "host_associated" class is broad (gut, skin, oral, infections, etc.). Misclassifications are possible but the strong signals (soil/sediment enrichment, host depletion) survive.
heading: Limitations

text: xoxF and PQQ presence or absence was assessed at gene-call level without checks for pseudogenes, truncated ORFs, or assembly fragmentation.
quote: **Sequence-level evidence is out of scope**: xoxF and PQQ presence/absence is at the gene-call level. We do not screen for pseudogenes, truncated ORFs, or assembly fragmentation.
heading: Limitations

text: Novel REE-handling enzymes lacking KEGG/RefSeq homologs would escape this annotation-based atlas.
quote: Genuinely novel REE-handling enzymes that lack KEGG/RefSeq homologs would not be detected.
heading: Limitations

quote: `kescience_bacdive`
